label: Formulated the Hatäta rationalist methodology
description: Zara Yaqob established an autonomous rationalist philosophy in the Hatäta, holding that God gave humans the light of reason to test all truth claims, reject sectarian bigotry, and construct an egalitarian moral life.
historicalContext: Written in 1667 in Ge'ez after Yaqob spent two years meditating in isolation in a cave near the Takkaze River to escape religious persecution.
dialecticalTension: Asserts the universality and supremacy of the natural light of reason over institutional ecclesiastical revelation and scriptural literalism.

citations.author: Zara Yaqob
citations.quote: God gave us reason so that we might investigate with it all things and judge what is good and what is evil.

citations.author: Claude Sumner
citations.work: Ethiopian Philosophy, vol. II: The Treatise of Zara Yaqob and Walda Heywat

label: Independent contemporaneous convergence on rationalist doubt and foundational epistemology
description: Contemporaneous with Descartes' Discourse on Method and Meditations, Yaqob developed an independent rationalist epistemology in Ethiopia, systematically doubting inherited dogmas and arriving at foundational rational certainty.
historicalContext: The 17th-century parallel emergence of rationalist critique in Western Europe and the Ethiopian Highlands without direct institutional contact.
dialecticalTension: Demonstrates that modern rationalist critique of scholastic authority was not a European monopoly, but a planetary intellectual emergence.

citations.author: Zara Yaqob
citations.quote: I thought in my heart: who is the judge of all these things? Is there someone who can distinguish truth from falsehood? I said to myself: it is the intellect that God has placed in us.

label: Established the African rationalist Enlightenment lineage
description: Yaqob's defense of autonomous reason, religious tolerance, and human equality established an intellectual precedent for the African philosophical Enlightenment carried forward by Anton Wilhelm Amo in 18th-century Europe.
historicalContext: The trans-epochal development of African rationalist philosophy confronting feudal dogma and racialized exclusion.
dialecticalTension: Bridges indigenous Nilotic rationalism with academic Enlightenment disputations in European universities.

citations.author: Kwame Anthony Appiah
citations.work: In My Father's House: Africa in the Philosophy of Culture
